We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the chain and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(xy) \\  & ={y}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x) \\  & ={y}^{2}\cdot (2x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y\cdot (1) \\  & =2x{y}^{2}+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(\frac{\pi }{4},2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(\frac{\pi }{4},2) & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}\cdot {2}^{2}+2\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot 2) \\  & =2\pi +2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =2\pi +2\end{aligned}
$$
